11116-the-wonderful-bed.title: The Wonderful Bed
11116-the-wonderful-bed.creator: Gertrude Knevels
11116-the-wonderful-bed.description: A book by Gertrude Knevels. The big bed in Aunt Jane's old nursery was the biggest and queerest the children had ever seen. It was the very opposite of the little white enameled beds they were used to sleeping in at their apartment in New York, being a great old-fashioned four-poster with a canopy almost touching the ceiling.

32584-the-secret-of-kralitz.title: The Secret Of Kralitz
32584-the-secret-of-kralitz.creator: Unknown
32584-the-secret-of-kralitz.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. last, "You have seen the ruins of the old monastery near the village, Franz. The first Baron burnt it and put the monks to the sword. The Abbot interfered too often with the Baron's whims. A girl sought shelter and the Abbot refused to give her up at the Baron's demand. His patience was at an end--you know the tales they still tell about him.

69920-holly-the-romance-of-a-southern-gi.title: _The Romance of a Southern Girl_
69920-holly-the-romance-of-a-southern-gi.creator: Ralph Henry Barbour
69920-holly-the-romance-of-a-southern-gi.description: A book by Ralph Henry Barbour. that when Captain Lamar Wayne died at Waynewood, in his fiftieth year, Holly, left quite alone in a suddenly empty world save for her father’s sister, Miss India Wayne, grieved passionately and rebelliously, giving way so abjectly to her sorrow that Aunt India, fearing gravely for her health, summoned the family physician.

arxiv-2107-05006.title: Green’s function related to a n n order linear differential equation coupled to arbitrary linear non local boundary conditions
arxiv-2107-05006.creator: Alberto Cabada, Lucía López-Somoza, Mouhcine Yousfi
arxiv-2107-05006.description: Abstract In this paper we obtain the explicit expression of the Green’s function related to a general n n order differential equation coupled to non-local linear boundary conditions. In such boundary conditions, a n n dimensional parameter dependence is also assumed. Moreover, some comparison principles are obtained.

arxiv-2111-01366.title: Improved Loss Function-Based Prediction Method of Extreme Temperatures in Greenhouses
arxiv-2111-01366.creator: Liao Qu, Shuaiqi Huang, Yunsong Jia, Xiang Li
arxiv-2111-01366.description: Abstract The prediction of extreme greenhouse temperatures to which crops are susceptible is essential in the field of greenhouse planting. It can help avoid heat or freezing damage and economic losses. Therefore, it’s important to develop models that can predict them accurately.

arxiv-2307-00421.title: Brightness-Restricted Adversarial Attack Patch
arxiv-2307-00421.creator: Mingzhen Shao
arxiv-2307-00421.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mingzhen Shao. Adversarial attack patches have gained increasing attention due to their practical applicability in physical-world scenarios. However, the bright colors used in attack patches represent a significant drawback, as they can be easily identified by human observers. Moreover, even though these attacks have been highly successful in deceiving target networks, which specific features of the attack patch contribute to its success are still unknown. Our paper introduces a brightness-restricted patch (BrPatch) that uses optical characteristics to effectively reduce conspicuousness while preserving image independence.

arxiv-2503-17009.title: Beautiful Exotica
arxiv-2503-17009.creator: Michał Praszałowicz
arxiv-2503-17009.description: Abstract The Chiral Quark–Soliton Model applied to baryons with one heavy quark predicts new exotic states belonging to three 𝟏𝟓 ¯ \overline{\boldsymbol{15}} SU(3) multiplets. Here, we extend previous analysis of charm exotica to the case of beauty. All model parameters are fixed from the charm sector and from the nonexotic b b –baryons.

arxiv-2505-21165.creator: Yansen Zhang 1 , Bowei He 1 , Xiaokun Zhang 1 , Haolun Wu 2 , Zexu Sun 3 , Chen Ma 1† 1 Department of Computer Science, City University of Hong Kong 2 School of Computer Science, McGill University 3 Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China yanszhang7-c@my.cityu.edu.hk ;

Existing recommender systems tend to prioritize items closely aligned with users’ historical interactions, inevitably trapping users in the dilemma of “filter bubble”.

arxiv-2510-27051.title: Adaptive Data Flywheel: Applying MAPE Control Loops to AI Agent Improvement
arxiv-2510-27051.creator: Aaditya Shukla, Sidney Knowles, Meenakshi Madugula, Dave Farris, Ryan Angilly, Santiago Pombo, Anbang Xu, Lu An, Abhinav Balasubramanian, Tan Yu, Jiaxiang Ren, Rama Akkiraju
arxiv-2510-27051.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aaditya Shukla, Sidney Knowles, Meenakshi Madugula, Dave Farris, Ryan Angilly, Santiago Pombo, Anbang Xu, Lu An, Abhinav Balasubramanian, Tan Yu, Jiaxiang Ren, Rama Akkiraju. Enterprise AI agents must continuously adapt to maintain accuracy, reduce latency, and remain aligned with user needs. We present a practical implementation of a data flywheel in NVInfo AI, NVIDIA’s Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Knowledge Assistant serving over 30,000 employees.

arxiv-2511-00215.creator: Xiaomeng Xu, Zahin Wahab, Reid Holmes, Caroline Lemieux
arxiv-2511-00215.description: Abstract . Code-documentation inconsistencies are common and undesirable: they can lead to developer misunderstandings and software defects. This paper introduces DocPrism , a multi-language, code-documentation inconsistency detection tool. DocPrism uses a standard large language model (LLM) to analyze and explain inconsistencies.

arxiv-2511-09281.creator: J. Haddad

arxiv-2601-10131.title: M 4 olGen: Multi-Agent, Multi-Stage Molecular Generation under Precise Multi-Property Constraints
arxiv-2601-10131.creator: Yizhan Li, Florence Cloutier, Sifan Wu, Ali Parviz, Boris Knyazev, Yan Zhang, Glen Berseth & Bang Liu
arxiv-2601-10131.description: Abstract Generating molecules that satisfy precise numeric constraints over multiple physicochemical properties is critical and challenging. Although large language models (LLMs) are expressive, they struggle with precise multi-objective control and numeric reasoning without external structure and feedback. We introduce M 4 olGen , a fragment-level, retrieval-augmented, two-stage framework for molecule generation under multi-property constraints.

pmc-10673555.title: Sterilized Polyhexanide-Releasing Chitosan Membranes with Potential for Use in Antimicrobial Wound Dressings
pmc-10673555.creator: Luís M Vaz, Rita Branco, Paula V Morais, António Jorge Guiomar
pmc-10673555.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Wound infection is a common complication of chronic wounds. It can impair healing, which may not occur without external help. Antimicrobial dressings (AMDs) are a type of external help to infected chronic wounds. In this study, highly porous membranes made of only chitosan and containing the antiseptic polyhexanide (poly(hexamethylene biguanide); PHMB) were prepared by cryogelation, aiming to be used in AMDs.

pmc-11431367.title: The Impact of Varying Lactose-to-Maltodextrin Ratios on the Physicochemical and Structural Characteristics of Pasteurized and Concentrated Skim and Whole Milk–Tea Blends
pmc-11431367.creator: Dilema Wijegunawardhana, Isuru Wijesekara, Rumesh Liyanage, Tuyen Truong, Mayumi Silva, Jayani Chandrapala
pmc-11431367.description: This study investigates the impact of substituting lactose with maltodextrin in milk–tea formulations to enhance their physicochemical and structural properties. Various lactose-to-maltodextrin ratios (100:0, 90:10, 85:15, 80:20, 75:25) were evaluated in both post-pasteurized and concentrated skim milk–tea (SM-T) and whole milk–tea (WM-T) formulations.

pmc-11671592.title: ErbB4 precludes the occurrence of PTSD-like fear responses by supporting the bimodal activity of the central amygdala
pmc-11671592.creator: Kibong Sung, Min-Jae Jeong, Taesik Yoo, Jung Hoon Jung, Sumin Kang, Jong-Yeon Yoo, Hyun Jin Kim, Kyunghyun Park, Jung Hyun Pyo, Hyun-Yong Lee, Noah Koo, Soo-Hee Choi, Joung-Hun Kim
pmc-11671592.description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) often arises after exposure to traumatic events and is characterized by dysregulated fear responses. Although the associations of erb-b2 receptor tyrosine kinase 4 (ErbB4) with various neuropsychiatric diseases, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, have been widely examined, the physiological roles of ErbB4 in PTSD and fear responses remain unclear.

pmc-12512089.title: Is Work‐Related Hearing Loss Associated With Dementia? Evidence From a High‐Risk Population
pmc-12512089.creator: Marianne Cloeren, John Dement, Jane Quackenbush, Patricia Quinn, Knut Ringen
pmc-12512089.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAge‐related hearing loss is associated with increased dementia risk. We examined the association between hearing loss and dementia in a population at high risk for hearing loss from occupational noise exposures.MethodsWe conducted cross‐sectional and longitudinal analyses using logistic regression and interval‐censored Cox models using data from the Building Trades National Medical Screening Program (BTMed), from inception in 1996 through March 2024.

pmc-12606852.title: Biological agents and plant growth regulator promote rice growth and regenerative capacity
pmc-12606852.creator: Hang Zhou, Lang Liu, Jianqun Zhou, Aibin He, Zhaohui Wu
pmc-12606852.description: Against the backdrop of global population and food demand growth, the development of ratoon rice is conducive to increasing food production and ensuring food security. Applying agricultural biotechnology and plant growth regulator to ratoon rice production is a key measure to promote the development of green agriculture and address the challenges of global food security.

pmc-12744758.title: Transport of secondary metabolites in plants: Mechanistic insights and transporter engineering for crop improvement
pmc-12744758.creator: Chunsheng Xiao, Gaofeng Zhou, Tianhua He, Chengdao Li
pmc-12744758.description: Secondary metabolites (SMs) are essential for plant survival and adaptation, playing multiple roles in ecological interactions such as defense and stress tolerance. Specialized transporters relocate SMs from their synthesis sites to defense tissues or storage organs. The spatiotemporal distribution of defense-related SMs is a key determinant of plant fitness.

pmc-13086936.title: Assessing farmers’ knowledge, attitudes, health risk perceptions, and practices toward pesticide use in Morocco
pmc-13086936.creator: Aziza Menouni, Imane Berni, Hala Chetouani, Said Abousaid, Kaoutar Chbihi, Ibrahim El Ghazi, Amal Amellah, Radu-Corneliu Duca, Samir El Jaafari, Lode Godderis
pmc-13086936.description: Agriculture plays a vital role in Africa’s economy, yet farmworkers remain disproportionately exposed to pesticide-related health risks. Guided by the Theory of Planned Behavior, this study examined farmworkers’ knowledge, attitudes, practices, and perceptions regarding health risks associated with pesticide use and protective measures in Morocco. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 314 agricultural workers across seven major farming areas.

pmc-13284154.title: Endometrial receptivity characteristics in patients with repeated implantation failure: a study using LASSO regression and Bayesian generalized linear model analysis
pmc-13284154.creator: Panpan Zhao, Yuexin Yu
pmc-13284154.description: BackgroundRepeated implantation failure (RIF) is a key challenge in assisted reproductive technology (ART), and its mechanism is closely related to Endometrial receptivity (ER). Although the effects of some Endometrial receptivity parameters on pregnancy outcomes have been investigated, there is a lack of standardized assessment of the interaction of multidimensional parameters and systematic prediction models.

pmc-13418203.title: Gestational age at birth and the risk of disability pension in early adulthood: a whole-population register study of people born in Finland in 1987–90
pmc-13418203.creator: Oksanen Päivi, Tikanmäki Marjaana, Alenius Suvi, Metsälä Johanna, Gissler Mika, Lahti-Pulkkinen Marius, Heikkilä Katriina, Räikkönen Katri, Ala-Mursula Leena, Kajantie Eero
pmc-13418203.description: BackgroundPreterm (<37 weeks), early-term (37–38 weeks), or post-term (42 weeks) birth may elevate the risk of mental, neurodevelopmental, and cardiopulmonary disease in adulthood, potentially impacting work capacity.MethodsWe examined the association between gestational age and early disability pension (DP) among 228 572 Finnish individuals born between 1 January 1987 and 30 September 1990.

pmc-13605416.creator: Andrea Matteucci, Michela Bonanni, Marco Valerio Mariani, Luca Sgarra, Lorenzo Nesti, Nicola Pierucci, Stefania Angela Di Fusco, Silvio Fedele, Federico Nardi, Furio Colivicchi
pmc-13605416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sudden cardiac death remains a major mode of cardiovascular mortality, yet the risk is neither constant over time nor adequately represented by left ventricular ejection fraction alone. The weeks after myocardial infarction and the early months after a new diagnosis of cardiomyopathy or acute myocarditis create arrhythmic vulnerability, and recovery with revascularization, guideline-directed medical therapy, rhythm control, or resolution of inflammation may render immediate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation unnecessary or inappropriate.

uslaw-usc-t25-s1680b.title: 25 U.S.C. § 1680b — National Health Service Corps
uslaw-usc-t25-s1680b.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s1680b.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 18 (Indian Health Care); Subchapter VI (Miscellaneous). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) No reduction in services The Secretary shall not remove a member of the National Health Service Corps from an Indian health program or urban Indian organization or withdraw funding used to support such a member, unless the Secretary, acting through the Service.
